Jack Ma admitted he knew nothing about technology or management when he started Alibaba. Instead of trying to master everything, he focused on finding people smarter than him in areas like computers and accounting. His philosophy was simple: leaders don't need to know it all-they need to bring the right people together. Smart individuals often struggle to collaborate, but with the right vision and leadership, they can create powerful results. This approach turned Alibaba from a small startup into a global giant valued at over $200 billion. Jack Ma's lesson: success is less about personal expertise and more about building teams that share a vision and work as one.#entrepreneurs #entrepreneurship #onlinebusinesstips #money #ecom

Ordering furniture from China isn’t as simple as finding a cute sofa on Alibaba and hitting “add to cart.” 😂 There’s a whole process between finding the furniture and having that container sitting at your warehouse. Manufacturers. Negotiations. Production. Freight. Customs. Port fees. Final delivery. And baby… there are PLENTY of opportunities to make an expensive mistake in between. Ask me how I know. 😭😂 I’ve been importing inventory for years, and learning how to source overseas completely changed the way I was able to grow my rental inventory. So if importing is something you’re seriously considering, learn the process BEFORE you start sending people your money. Busca proveedores verificados: revisa su antigüedad, certificaciones y perfil. ✅ 2. Utiliza Trade Assurance: paga siempre dentro de Alibaba y revisa las condiciones de protección. ✅ 3. No te dejes llevar por el precio más barato: si una oferta parece demasiado buena para ser verdad, investiga. ✅ 4. Solicita muestras: verifica la calidad antes de invertir en grandes cantidades. ✅ 5. Pide una videollamada: solicita ver la fábrica, los productos y las instalaciones. ✅ 6.
